regions.name: Central Plains (中原)
regions.description: Henan, Shandong, Hubei - Heart of civilization and orthodox martial traditions.

regions.name: Guanzhong & Northwest (关中·西北)
regions.description: Shaanxi, Shanxi, Gansu, Ningxia - Imperial valleys, passes, and Silk Road.

regions.name: Bashu & Southwest (巴蜀·西南)
regions.description: Sichuan, Chongqing, Yunnan, Guizhou, Guangxi - Mist mountains and martial hermitages.

regions.name: Jiangnan & South (江南·岭南)
regions.description: Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Anhui, Jiangxi, Fujian, Guangdong - Rich waterways and merchant guilds.

regions.name: Northern Steppe & Frontier (塞北·西域)
regions.description: Inner Mongolia, Xinjiang, Tibet, Qinghai - Boundless expanses and demonic legends.

regions.name: Guandong / Northeast (关东·东北)
regions.description: Liaoning, Jilin, Heilongjiang - Frozen forests, wild rivers, and iron cavalry.

provinces.name: Gansu
provinces.description: The slender martial artery connecting the Central Plains to the Silk Road. Guarded by the swordmasters of Mount Kongtong and Jiayu Pass.

provinces.name: Qinghai
provinces.description: Vast, wind-swept high plateau sheltering the mother waters of both the Yangtze and Yellow Rivers. Gateway to the mystical Kunlun.

provinces.name: Guangxi
provinces.description: Dramatic karst tooth mountains rising from jade waters. The deep jungle mountains have long been a refuge for unorthodox and tribal clans.

provinces.name: Guizhou
provinces.description: Rugged highland plateau famous for Mount Fanjing, perilous gorges, and mystifying medicinal herbalists.

provinces.name: Chongqing
provinces.description: The cliffside metropolis where the Jialing joins the Yangtze. Diaoyu Fortress was renowned as an impregnable bastion against invading Mongol hordes.

provinces.name: Beijing
provinces.description: Seat of the Dragon Throne and the Emperor's Guard (Embroidered Uniform Guard / Jinyiwei). Where imperial politics clashes with the martial underworld.

provinces.name: Fujian
provinces.description: Maritime springboard with rugged coastal red sandstones. The secluded gorges of Mount Wuyi conceal hermit pavilions and hidden scrolls.

provinces.name: Anhui
provinces.description: Domain of granite cliffs and ancient pine seas at Mount Huang. Renowned for wealthy merchant associations and Buddhist sanctuaries.

provinces.name: Guangdong
provinces.description: Southernmost martial world trading hub. Known for southern fist traditions, maritime merchant fleets, and prosperous guild halls.

provinces.name: Tibet
provinces.description: The roof of the world. Towering permafrost peaks, esoteric lama martial disciplines, vajra fist traditions, and sacred holy lakes.

provinces.name: Xinjiang
provinces.description: The boundless Western Regions. The cradle of the Heavenly Demon Cult legends, Kunlun sword sanctums, and forgotten oasis kingdoms.

provinces.name: Hainan
provinces.description: The tropical southern frontier. Ancient place of exile for deposed scholars and martial recluses, surrounded by turquoise coral seas.

provinces.name: Ningxia
provinces.description: Ancient realm of the Western Xia dynasty. Rugged Helan Mountain crests shielded martial academies from fierce desert sandstorms.

provinces.name: Shaanxi
provinces.description: The ancient cradle of emperors and martial legends. Home to the legendary Mount Hua and the Guanzhong plains surrounded by impregnable mountain passes.

provinces.name: Shanxi
provinces.description: Land west of the Taihang Mountains. Guarded by the strategic Yanmen Pass and Mount Wutai, a sacred Buddhist sanctuary.

provinces.name: Hubei
provinces.description: Sacred mountain realm and fortress crossroads. Famous for Mount Wudang and the legendary fortified gates of Xiangyang on the Han River.

provinces.name: Hunan
provinces.description: Vast realm of misty lakes and jagged quartz sandstone peaks. Dongting Lake was historically controlled by formidable water bandits and beggar sects.

provinces.name: Sichuan
provinces.description: The fortress basin of abundance, enclosed by sheer cliffs. Celebrated for mystical Daoist heights and secretive poison master clans.

provinces.name: Yunnan
provinces.description: The romantic, secluded kingdom of Dian and Dali. Towering snow peaks, six finger sword qi legends, and southern border caravans.

provinces.name: Hebei
provinces.description: Land of heroic swordsmen and staunch northern defenders. Gateway to the northern frontier and guardian of the Imperial Capital.

provinces.name: Henan
provinces.description: The beating heart of Zhongyuan (Central Plains) and historical pivot of the martial world. Site of ancient dynasties and Mount Song.

provinces.name: Liaoning
provinces.description: The fortified threshold "Beyond the Pass" (Guandong). Northern iron cavalry, dense forests, and fierce mountain warrior tribes.

provinces.name: Shandong
provinces.description: Home of Mount Tai, the foremost sacred mountain where emperors offered sacrifices to Heaven. Rich martial arts lineage and coastal ports.

provinces.name: Tianjin
provinces.description: The imperial ferry outpost guarding the sea entrance to the capital. Renowned in martial arts lore for street challenges and martial halls.

provinces.name: Jiangxi
landmarks: Mount Longhu (Dragon-Tiger Mountain Daoist Ancestral Hall)
provinces.description: Flanked by Poyang Lake and Mount Lu. Longhu Mountain served as the supreme seat of Celestial Master Daoism and talismanic arts.

provinces.name: Jiangsu
provinces.description: The wealthy cultural crown of Jiangnan. Waterway hubs, flourishing mercantile guilds, and southern imperial prestige.

provinces.name: Shanghai
provinces.description: Estuary where the colossal Yangtze meets the East China Sea. Key transit point for coastal smuggling, salt guilds, and foreign merchant junks.

provinces.name: Zhejiang
provinces.description: Southern capital realm of serene West Lake, coastal pilgrimage islands, and legendary sword-smithing furnaces at Mount Mogan.

provinces.name: Jilin
provinces.description: Crowned by the eternal snow-capped volcanic crater of Mount Changbai. Known for century-old wild ginseng and northern frost martial arts.

provinces.name: Inner Mongolia
provinces.description: The roaring ocean of grass ruled by nomadic mounted archers and eagle tamers. Across history, the great northern rival of Central Plains warriors.

provinces.name: Heilongjiang
provinces.description: The northern wilderness. Endless primeval pine forests and frozen rivers where hardy survivalist clans forged unyielding frost blades.

provinces.name: Taiwan
provinces.description: The maritime fortress isle across the Taiwan Strait. Controlled historically by pirate confederacies, merchant princes, and island tribes.

provinces.name: Hong Kong
provinces.description: Sheltered deepwater islands formerly infested with pirate flotillas and maritime martial trade brotherhoods.

provinces.name: Macau
provinces.description: The Lotus Isle where western firearms and esoteric clockwork artifacts entered the Central Plains through maritime traders.

mountains.name: Mount Song (Songshan)
mountains.description: The Central Sacred Mountain of China. Towering over Dengfeng in Henan; supreme focal point of martial cultivation and Zen arts.

mountains.name: Mount Hua (Huashan)
mountains.description: The Western Sacred Mountain. Famous for sheer vertical granite precipices, Plank Walk in the Sky, and the legendary Huashan Sword Contests.

mountains.name: Mount Tai (Taishan)
mountains.description: The Eastern Sacred Mountain and most revered peak under heaven. Where dozens of emperors conducted the solemn Feng Shan sacrifices to Heaven.

mountains.name: Mount Wudang
mountains.description: Supreme Daoist sanctuary of internal martial arts, Taiji, and swordplay nestled amid 72 mist-shrouded peaks and cloud terraces.

mountains.name: Mount Emei
mountains.description: Towering Buddhist sanctuary overlooking the Sichuan basin with its Golden Summit, sea of clouds, and sacred golden Buddha statues.

mountains.name: Mount Qingcheng
mountains.description: Birthplace of religious Daoism in Sichuan, famed as the "most secluded mountain under heaven" with emerald jade pavilions.

mountains.name: Mount Heng (North)
mountains.description: Northern Sacred Mountain guarding the frontier passes. Features the miraculous Hanging Monastery clinging to a sheer cliff.

mountains.name: Mount Heng (South)
mountains.description: Southern Sacred Mountain of emerald forests, 72 peaks, and flying smoke waterfalls above the Xiang River valley.

mountains.name: Mount Huang (Huangshan)
mountains.description: The ethereal Yellow Mountain with gnarled Welcoming Pines, seas of cloud, bizarre granite monoliths, and thermal hot springs.

mountains.name: Mount Wuyi
mountains.description: Red sandstone gorges and tea plantations flanking the meandering Nine-Bend River; home to hermits, scholars, and Daoist recluses.

mountains.name: Mount Longhu
mountains.description: Dragon and Tiger Mountain; historic ancestral seat of Celestial Master Daoism, ancient cliff coffins, and talisman magic.

mountains.name: Mount Changbai (Heaven Lake)
mountains.description: Massive active volcano crater filled by deep sapphire waters, sacred mountain of northeastern warrior tribes and frost qi masters.

mountains.name: Kunlun Peak (Ancestral Mountain)
mountains.description: The mythological ancestral root of all mountain chains under heaven, immortal realm of the Queen Mother of the West (Xi Wangmu).

mountains.name: Heavenly Mountain (Tianshan Bogda)
mountains.description: Snow-crested Bogda peak looming above Heavenly Lake (Tianchi), famed home of supreme sword techniques and lotus herbs.

mountains.name: Mount Kongtong
mountains.description: Sacred mountain on the Silk Road where the Yellow Emperor historically asked the Dao from hermit Guangchengzi.

mountains.name: Hangu Pass
mountains.description: Ancient choke point bottleneck between Luoyang and Chang'an. Where Laozi wrote the Dao De Jing before riding into the west.

mountains.name: Shanhaiguan
mountains.description: First Pass Under Heaven (天下第一关). Where the Great Wall meets the Bohai Sea. Strategic gateway between the Central Plains and Guandong.

mountains.name: Jiayuguan
mountains.description: First Strategic Pass of the West (天下第一雄关). Western terminus of the Great Wall along the Silk Road.

mountains.name: Jianmen Pass
mountains.description: Sword Gate. Sheer sandstone cleft in northern Sichuan: "One man can hold the pass against ten thousand attackers."

mountains.name: Yanmen Pass
mountains.description: Wild Goose Gate. Perilous gorge in the Yanmen Mountains, historic frontline between the steppe and Central Plains.
